decisions.reason: Although the particle therapy phantom had a delayed US launch and lower web prominence, the firm has already invested in its development and publicized it, so escalation of commitment makes a drop unlikely in the next year.
As a specialized small-volume chamber central to modern radiotherapy QA, its sunk costs and public commitment outweigh any temporary visibility gaps, leading management to persist.
The second small-volume chamber shares the firm's investment in this dosimetry segment, and management sees its continued presence as justified by earlier commitments.
The standard clinical ionization chamber line is a core, highly visible product family with substantial sunk investments, making withdrawal highly unlikely under escalation of commitment.
Relative dosimetry chambers are central to the firm's calibration and QA portfolio, so prior investments and public commitments support keeping the product.
The thimble chamber represents established technology in which the firm has committed resources, and disappointing signals are still attributable to temporary external factors.
